3.4 JOINTPOLICY–SKILLCO-EVOLUTION
At each training step, actor rollouts and skill proposals are generated from the same pre-update policy
and skillbank snapshot. We jointly optimize the shared policy by minimizing
LUniSkill =L actor +λ propLproposer,(16)
whereλprop weights the proposer loss. A positive Ralign indicates a wider action log-likelihood
gap between successful and failed references, even if likelihoods decrease on both. For skillbank
updates, however, we adopt a stricter criterion by additionally requiring ∆+ >0 to avoid storing
skills that reduce the average action log-likelihood on the successful reference. After the policy
update, we apply ADDand UPDATEproposals that pass both critic checks and satisfy ∆+ >0 and
Ralign >0 . For each UPDATEtarget, we apply the eligible proposal with the highest Ralign. The
complete training procedure is summarized in Algorithm 1 in Appendix C.
4 EXPERIMENTS
4.1 EXPERIMENTALSETUP
Benchmarks.We evaluate UniSkill on ALFWorld (Shridhar et al., 2021) and WebShop (Yao et al.,
2022), two multi-turn interactive benchmarks. ALFWorld requires agents to complete household
tasks through text-based navigation and object manipulation. We report per-task-type and overall
success rates. WebShop requires an agent to search, inspect, and purchase products that satisfy a
natural-language instruction in a simulated e-commerce website. We report the mean normalized task
score, scaled to 100, and the success rate.
Baselines and Implementation Details.We compare UniSkill with training-free, RL-only, and
memory- or skill-augmented RL baselines. All compared methods use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Yang
et al., 2024) as the base model. Unless otherwise specified, the baseline results in Table 1 are
drawn from prior work (Feng et al., 2025; Shi et al., 2026), where they were obtained using the
releasedVERL-AGENTimplementations (Feng et al., 2025) under a common evaluation protocol. We
evaluate UniSkill using the same protocol, including ALFWorld’s officialvalid seen split, task-
